title: Prove Feuerbach distance relations via coordinate computation

problemStatement.plain: The nine-point circle is tangent to the incircle and all three excircles. Core distance relations: |NI| = |R/2 - r| and |NI_a| = R/2 + r_a.

proven: All 9 points on nine-point circle (3 midpoints, 3 Euler midpoints, 3 altitude feet)

blockers: Incenter formula uses sqrt side lengths - nested sqrt makes field_simp/ring approach intractable
Need alternative approach: complex coordinates, inversive geometry, or power-of-point
currentState.nextAction: Explore squaring approach for general Feuerbach or Mathlib inner-product reformulation

insights: General Feuerbach distance proofs blocked by sqrt in side lengths: incenter coords involve a=sqrt(...), cross terms a*b resist ring tactic
NI = R/2 - r (Feuerbach incircle tangency) follows from Euler identity, but proving either requires eliminating sqrt

The equilateral_R_eq_2r proof in main file was broken by Mathlib v4.26 upgrade (dist2_sq unfold change) - independently proved in OQ01
Approach for general case: introduce a^2, b^2, c^2 as polynomial constraints and use nlinarith - untested but promising
Extended law of sines (squared) IS provable as polynomial identity - key was rw [sq_abs] to eliminate |x|² before ring
General Feuerbach proof chain: ext_law_of_sines → sigma_identity → Euler OI²=R²-2Rr → NI=(R/2-r)
FUNDAMENTAL OBSTACLE: incenter coords involve side_a/side_b/side_c (sqrt). Products a·b resist ring. Need reformulation without sqrt or algebraic elimination.
